## `8025768` — knowledge: add preclinical metadata knowledge graph + grounding (Milestone A)
<sub>2026-06-23 · Claude · scope `knowledge` · 9 file(s)</sub>

> Lightweight, ontology-bound KG that grounds metadata reasoning for cloud and
> local LLMs and suggests ontology IRIs for recognised biological values. Fully
> offline; online IRI resolution is opt-in (ENABLE_ONLINE_ENRICHMENT).
>
> Derived from the precliniverse "Open Science Dataset Registration Wizard"
> schema (vendored under backend/knowledge/sources/ with attribution):
> ontology-bound entity types (organism→NCBITaxon, strain/diet→EFO,
> molecule→ChEBI, disease→DOID, tissue→UBERON, gene/allele, DataCite fields),
> 15 model-organism presets with NCBITaxon IRIs, CRediT roles, and the resolver
> API registry.
>
> - backend/knowledge/: preclinical_kg.yaml (curated runtime KG), kg.py (loader),
>   retriever.py (deterministic column→concept matching by name OR value,
>   grounding_block(), suggest_iris()), README.
> - Retrieval-augmented injection: grounding_block() is added to the LLM system
>   blocks in llm_column_enricher (cached alongside the validated vocabulary), so
>   it works without relying on local-model tool-calling.
> - uri_suggester now emits additive `ontology_suggestions` (exact offline IRIs
>   for known controlled values, e.g. Mus musculus → NCBITaxon_10090; otherwise a
>   scheme-level resolver hint).
> - Tests: test_knowledge_kg.py (9) cover loading, name/value matching, grounding
>   block content, and exact/hint IRI suggestion.
>
> Value: with blinded headers the KG recovers species/strain/molecule/tissue from
> values alone — the signal that lifts the harness's blind-mode accuracy.

- **Why:** Milestone A — metadata reasoning needed grounding in a real preclinical knowledge graph, not just template strings.
- **How:** Added backend/knowledge/ (KG from the precliniverse schema) with a deterministic retriever that injects per-column subgraphs + offline ontology IRIs (NCBITaxon/UBERON/UO).
- **Impact:** Foundation for grounded, hallucination-resistant metadata suggestions; offline by design.
- **Tags:** grant, milestone-A, knowledge-graph

## `77f158b` — backend: add provider-agnostic LLM layer + grant roadmap (Milestone B)
<sub>2026-06-23 · Claude · scope `backend` · 9 file(s)</sub>

> Foundational step for running FAIR-VCG Mentor on a locally-hosted LLM

> Swiss 3RCC grant. Adds docs/grant-roadmap.md mapping all milestones to
> concrete workstreams.
>
> LLM provider abstraction (llm_service.py):

>   and dict return, so all 10 call sites are provider-agnostic.
> - openai path drives local models via structured-output JSON-schema
>   (response_format built from the tool input_schema), falling back to

>   Layer-2 gate now uses llm_enabled() instead of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
>
> CrossRef/DOI lookup is now gated behind ENABLE_ONLINE_ENRICHMENT (off by
> default) so the default deployment is fully offline.

> Config: add openai to requirements; add backend/.env.example documenting the

> JSON parsing, PDF-block flattening, and call_haiku dispatch under both
> providers (no network).

- **Why:** Milestone B — the tool was coupled to Anthropic; the grant requires running fully on a local LLM with no external API.
- **How:** Added a provider switch (anthropic|openai/LM Studio) in llm_service with a structured-output local path and local PDF→text; provider_info() reports state; CrossRef gated behind ENABLE_ONLINE_ENRICHMENT.
- **Impact:** Single provider seam; the whole app can run offline against Gemma/APERTUS.

## `f237351` — fix: report all ARRIVE/PREPARE occurrences, not just first unique match
<sub>2026-05-29 · Claude · scope `fix` · 3 file(s)</sub>

> The previous _find_matches used a global seen_lower set across all pages,
> which caused every occurrence after the first unique matched string to be
> silently skipped. A document with 93 ARRIVE citations would show only ~10.
>
> Fix: replace global text deduplication with per-page span-based deduplication.
> Only prevents two overlapping regex patterns from double-counting the same
> character position on the same page (e.g. \bARRIVE 2.0\b and \bARRIVE\b
> hitting the same span). Every occurrence on every page is now reported.
>
> Also adds total_occurrences to the detect_citations output, surfaces it in
> the results table chip ("Cited (93×)") and in the CSV export column
> arrive_occurrences / prepare_occurrences.
>
> https://claude.ai/code/session_01TxFnFKTFpRQjsssKoyYvXv

## `cf8fa96` — feat: add two-layer NTS citation analyser
<sub>2026-05-29 · Claude · scope `feat` · 8 file(s)</sub>

> Adds a deterministic + optional LLM pipeline for analysing Non-Technical
> Summary (NTS) PDFs to detect ARRIVE and PREPARE guideline citations and
> extract structured metadata.
>
> Layer 1 (always on): pdfminer.six text extraction + compiled regex patterns
> covering DOIs, full titles, author-year citations, and ALL-CAPS acronyms for
> both ARRIVE (8 patterns, including Kilkenny and Percie du Sert author forms)
> and PREPARE (6 patterns, including Norecopa and Smith et al.). Uppercase-only
> matching for acronyms prevents false positives from the verbs "arrive" / "prepare".
> Every match records exact text, page number, and confidence tier.
>
> Layer 2 (optional, requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY): forced Anthropic tool-call
> schema extracts 22 NTS-specific metadata fields mapped to ARRIVE 2.0 and
> PREPARE field IDs (species, severity, 3Rs, harm-benefit, lay summary, etc.).
> Uses native PDF base64 input with ephemeral prompt caching.
>
> New files: backend/nts_analyzer.py, backend/nts_router.py,
>   frontend/src/pages/NTSAnalyzerPage.tsx
> Modified: main.py (router registration), requirements.txt (pdfminer.six),
>   App.tsx (route), Layout.tsx (nav item + icon), api/client.ts (API helpers)
>
> Endpoints: POST /api/nts/analyze, POST /api/nts/analyze-batch,
>   GET /api/nts/export/{id}/csv, GET /api/nts/export/{id}/json
>
> https://claude.ai/code/session_01TxFnFKTFpRQjsssKoyYvXv

- **Why:** Reviewers and grant evidence benefit from analysing the citation/NTS context of a paper.
- **How:** Added a two-layer NTS (non-technical summary) citation analyser.
- **Impact:** Extracts 3Rs/procedure/harm-benefit context from papers; feeds the metadata and VCG flows.
- **Tags:** nts, feature

>
> 1. PREPARE-only paper hints never reached the Template Fill UI.
>    _lookup_paper_value (template_engine) reads only the arrive and
>    dataset_metadata blocks; the new paper_extraction["prepare"] block
>    from paper_extractor.py was never consulted, so template fields like
>    prepare_literature_searches / prepare_facility_inspection /
>    prepare_necropsy_plan came back with paper_hint=None even when the
>    extractor had populated them. The "use paper hint" affordance was a
>    no-op for the PREPARE-only side of the checklist.
>
>    Fix lives in template_completion.py — a _PREPARE_HINT_MAP table maps
>    the 42 PREPARE template field_ids onto the 13 topic-level extraction
>    keys (multiple sub-items share one extracted topic). Both
>    _paper_hint_for_field and fill_from_paper_extraction fall through to
>    the new map when the original lookup returns nothing, with
>    fill_from_paper_extraction stamping a "prepare.<topic_key>" source
>    path so the UI can show provenance.
>
> 2. Editing an LLM/document suggestion silently dropped it. The drawer
>    open path in editSuggestion removed the pending suggestion from the
>    queue before the user had a chance to save — cancelling the drawer
>    lost the suggestion forever. Now the suggestion stays in the queue
>    until handleDrawerSave succeeds for that field_id.
>
> Two new regression tests (paper_hint surfacing + bulk-fill from
> prepare block); full template suite 24/24 green.
>
> https://claude.ai/code/session_01RysbM1wi9ynR4sp1pHFJRt

## `83771d4` — templates: add NAMO assay template + LinkML schema importer
<sub>2026-05-14 · Claude · scope `templates` · 7 file(s)</sub>

> Phase 5 — extends the template layer to support LinkML-based ontologies (NAMO,
> and any future LinkML schema).
>
> Hand-crafted template:
> - templates/namo-nam-assay-v1.yaml: NAMO NAM dose-response / functional assay
>   template targeting the realistic CSV shape (compound x concentration x
>   endpoint). Maps to NAMO LinkML classes Study, NAMModel, FunctionalAssay, and
>   DoseResponseSimilarity via class_iri_map. Declares vcg_defaults
>   (compound_id as treatment, response_value as outcome) and a
>   dose_response_summary predefined analysis.
>
> LinkML importer (linkml_import.py):
> - linkml_to_template(schema, target_class) walks the LinkML classes/attributes
>   blocks (resolving is_a chains) and produces a starter FAIR-VCG template.
> - target_class=None mode picks data-like classes (numeric-attribute presence or
>   *Result|Assay|Metric* naming) and emits required_metadata; abstract and
>   purely structural classes (NamedThing, Reference, Term) are skipped.
> - target_class set mode emits required_columns from that class's flattened
>   attributes; numeric ranges become semantic_type=measurement.
> - Always populates class_iri_map for downstream JSON-LD export.
> - Output passes META_SCHEMA validation; clean ValueError on bad YAML or
>   missing target class.
>
> Endpoint: POST /api/templates/import-linkml accepts {linkml_yaml,
> target_class, save_as_user_template} and returns the generated template dict +
> serialized YAML preview. Optionally persists to backend/templates/user/.
>
> Frontend: TemplateSelectorPage gains a second upload card "Import from LinkML
> schema" with textarea, target-class input, save-now checkbox, and inline
> preview of the generated YAML.
>
> Tests: 9 new in tests/test_linkml_import.py covering full-schema conversion,
> target-class extraction for FunctionalAssay and DoseResponseSimilarity,
> class_iri_map population, is_a flattening, bad-input rejection, and a match
> score for a screening CSV against the hand-crafted NAMO template. Suite now
> 116 passed.
>
> API contract additions:
> - POST /api/templates/import-linkml — new endpoint.
> - Imported templates can be saved as user templates via the same upload path
>   (no new persistence surface).
>
> https://claude.ai/code/session_01UBg63TBnW9CLdqbSF5R3tM

>   session["template_candidates"] added.

- **Impact:** Template-driven conformance + the hierarchical conforms_to model used by every later standard.

## `258135e` — vcg+scoring+hitl: vocabulary-constrained LLM calls + versioning + PDF discovery
<sub>2026-05-14 · Claude · scope `misc` · 14 file(s)</sub>

> Adds a per-session controlled vocabulary (column names, semantic types,
> units, metadata keys, controlled values, licenses, study types) that
> every Haiku call is constrained to. Tool input schemas are built
> dynamically with enums drawn from the vocabulary, and the validated
> vocabulary is injected as a cached system-prompt block.
>
> HITL suggestions are stamped with the schema_version they were created
> against. Validating the vocabulary or approving a schema_extension bumps
> the version and marks older pending/edited suggestions as stale so the
> user knows they need re-generation.
>
> New schema_extension HITL category + PDF discovery endpoint mines a
> paper for vocabulary additions, gated by user approval before they
> enter the controlled vocabulary.
>
> TODO follow-ups added: structural schema verification on validate,
> per-field template reuse, ontology lookup (OLS/BioPortal), vocabulary
> diff view, text-mode discovery, auto-stale on column edits, in-place
> re-suggestion for stale cards.
>
> https://claude.ai/code/session_01F1FkyuQekxkTemVtmcfYK1

- **Why:** LLM suggestions must be controlled and auditable, not free-form.
- **How:** Vocabulary-constrained LLM calls with versioning + a human-in-the-loop (HITL) review queue + PDF vocab discovery.
- **Impact:** Every AI suggestion is enum-constrained and human-approved before it lands — the grant's stated safeguard pattern.
- **Tags:** hitl, llm, vocabulary

## `fd28bca` — profiler: implement column-understanding roadmap stages 0-2
<sub>2026-05-07 · Claude · scope `profiler` · 12 file(s)</sub>

> Stage 0 (benchmark and gates):
> - Extend benchmark with confidence-bucket distribution and
>   per-misclassification report so reviewers can see where rules fall
>   short, not just an aggregate score.
>
> Stage 1 (deterministic uplift):
> - Move synonym dictionaries to vcg/constants.py and broaden them with
>   clinical-chemistry markers (ALT/AST/ALP/LDH/BUN/CRP), preclinical
>   unit suffixes (_u_l, _iu_l, _mmol_l, …), sex/strain keyword banks,
>   and ARRIVE-style dotted column conventions.
> - Add value-shape validators (identifier regex match, date parsing,
>   numeric coupling, categorical cardinality) that combine with name
>   patterns to calibrate confidence and emit a `reason_codes` audit
>   trail per column.  Conflicts (e.g. unit-suffixed name with
>   non-numeric values) are flagged explicitly.
> - Cover all four test_data CSVs with end-to-end inference assertions
>   plus targeted unit tests for the new validators and reason codes.
>   Benchmark now reports 33/33 correct (100%) with all Stage 0 gates
>   passing.
>
> Stage 2 (template memory + correction tracking):
> - New template_store module persists user-confirmed column mappings
>   keyed by a stable dataset signature (sorted-name SHA-256 prefix)
>   in the existing SQLite store.  Upload auto-applies a saved template
>   when the signature matches and surfaces the count of low-confidence
>   columns (confidence < 0.65) so the wizard can prompt only where it
>   needs to.
> - Track type/label/unit corrections per session as Stage 2 acceptance
>   metrics; expose via GET /api/templates/{id}.
> - Frontend: surface the low-confidence prompt as a warning banner
>   with click-to-edit chips, highlight low-confidence rows in the
>   column table, and add a Save-as-template action.  Update Zustand
>   state and API client to carry the new fields end-to-end.

## `ae0a2c5` — feat(vcg): complete VCG pipeline — orchestrator, engine, report, router, and frontend pages
<sub>2026-05-01 · Claude · scope `misc` · 12 file(s)</sub>

> Implements the full Virtual Control Group feature end-to-end:
>
> Backend:
> - vcg/orchestrator.py: HITL state-machine (8-state conversation flow) that asks
>   contextual questions based on actual column names/values from the profiler
> - vcg/vcg_engine.py: pipeline runner (DataIngestion → Standardization → VCG build →
>   Stats), async-safe via asyncio.to_thread, auto-selects bootstrap (N≥15) or
>   synthetic (N<15) method
> - vcg/vcg_report.py: Markdown report generator with covariate balance table,
>   outcome comparison, power analysis, reliability assessment, and 3Rs justification
> - vcg/vcg_router.py: FastAPI APIRouter with dependency injection (init_vcg_router),
>   endpoints for wizard, chat, generate, status, results, and CSV/report export
> - vcg/agents/stats_agent.py: KS tests, Cohen's d, power analysis, SMD balance,
>   diagnostic plots (KDE overlay + Q-Q) as base64 PNG
> - vcg/agents/vcg_synthetic.py: KDE/Normal sampling with Shapiro-Wilk lognormality
>   detection for small control groups
> - Updated main.py to register vcg_router and wire shared session store
> - Updated requirements.txt: scipy, statsmodels, pingouin, matplotlib
>
> Frontend:
> - pages/VCGWizardPage.tsx: 4-step MUI Stepper wizard (prefill + validation)
> - pages/VCGResultsPage.tsx: results dashboard with reliability badge, covariate
>   balance table, outcome charts (Recharts), diagnostic plots, and export buttons
> - App.tsx: added /vcg, /vcg/wizard, /vcg/results routes
> - Layout.tsx: added VCG Wizard and VCG Results nav items with ScienceIcon/BarChartIcon
>
> Smoke test passes: ingestion, standardization, bootstrap VCG, stats, report
> (reliability score 0.871, KS p-values body_weight_g=0.75, glucose_AUC=0.435)
>
> https://claude.ai/code/session_01418kV9jrVjvgMtutAs9xZf

- **Why:** Core product feature — generate statistically rigorous virtual control groups without an external LLM.
- **How:** Added the full VCG module — rule-based orchestrator FSM, four-agent engine, Markdown report, router, and frontend pages.
- **Impact:** The VCG half of the product; everything in the grant's VCG/3Rs story builds on this.
- **Tags:** vcg, feature

## `80aaf82` — Initial implementation of FAIR CSV Mentor
<sub>2026-04-30 · damien huzard · scope `misc` · 29 file(s)</sub>

> Full-stack educational tool for FAIR-readiness assessment of CSV files.
>
> Backend (FastAPI + Python):
> - CSV profiler: encoding/delimiter detection, semantic column typing, unit guessing
> - Entity detector: table shape inference (repeated measures, wide, long format)
> - FAIR engine: rule-based scoring across Findable/Accessible/Interoperable/Reusable
> - Export engine: cleaned CSV, data dictionary, Frictionless, CSVW, JSON-LD, Markdown report, RO-Crate 1.2 ZIP
> - 14 REST endpoints with in-memory session store
>
> Frontend (React 18 + Vite + TypeScript + MUI v6):
> - 6-page guided workflow: Upload → Overview → Column Profile → FAIR Score → Metadata Wizard → Export
> - Drag-and-drop CSV upload with immediate analysis
> - Expandable issue cards with "why it matters" and "suggested fix" explanations
> - Interactive column editor (label, description, unit, allowed values, URI)
> - FAIR score breakdown with per-dimension criteria checklist
> - One-click download for all 8 export formats including RO-Crate ZIP
